subject: Critical: Brightleaf websocket multiplex stalls — request for cross-team war room
messages:
From: Lauren Cho <laurencho@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brightleafhealth.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:13:22 -0800
Subject: Live sessions freezing under concurrency — attaching traces

Hi Tessa,

We're seeing repeated live session freezes in our integration tests and this morning on production. Symptoms: websocket sessions appear to accept input but then stall mid-response (~45-75s after start) with no additional chunks; clients eventually get a connection reset or a 504. This happens sporadically but correlates with sustained concurrency above ~180 parallel WS connections.

We captured a short pcap and the client-side error traces (attached). Example: when the model is asked a multi-turn prompt, the stream will produce a handful of chunks, then stop sending further tokens despite the backend showing activity for the request ID. After ~30-60s the client sees the socket closed.

Impact: several Brightleaf QA sessions timed out and one pilot user reported a degraded experience. This is blocking our expansion pilot with the care team — want this on your radar as high priority.

I've attached a pcap and a small set of logs. Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Lauren Cho
Sr. Platform Engineer, Brightleaf Health

Attachments: capture-2027-02-11-brightleaf.pcap (pcap), client-errors.log (txt)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:44:37 -08:00
Subject: Re: Live sessions freezing under concurrency — attaching traces

Quick triage notes from runtime/infra:
- Reproduced locally against the same session IDs. The runtime continues to show request processing (tokens being generated) but the network layer (our edge proxy) is intermittently stopping chunked transfer encoding frames for these connections. There are correlated 502s from the proxy during the same minute window.
- Initial hypothesis: under sustained multiplexed websocket load we see kernel-selection slowdowns that allow the proxy's per-connection write buffer to back up; when the buffer hits the threshold we see the proxy close the stream or drop the chunked flush.

Immediate mitigation we can roll out in minutes:
- Temporarily disable multiplexing (ws session-level multiplexing) for Brightleaf. This forces each inference request to use a dedicated connection/route and avoids the shared write-buffer contention.
- Add a short-lived autoscale bump (one dedicated slot) to absorb burst while we observe.

I'll attach a small diff to disable mux for the customer and a snippet of the proxy logs. If we disable mux we should see chunked frames resume uninterrupted.

Attachments: mux-disable-diff.patch (diff), proxy-502-snippets.txt (txt)

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:12:04 -08:00
Subject: Exec summary + proposed customer remediation (Brightleaf)

Laura / leadership team — short exec update so you can see proposed next steps and an ask for customer-facing concessions:
- What happened: During a sustained burst (~200+ concurrent WS sessions) Brightleaf experienced intermittent chunked-transfer stalls likely caused by write-buffer contention at the edge proxy that surfaces when websocket multiplexing is active. The runtime continues to generate tokens but the proxy is aborting chunked flushes.
- Immediate action taken: Karthik's team has prepared a mux-disable config and proxy log snippets (attached). Tessa has opened INF-8721 for tracking. We're proposing an immediate deployment of the mux-disable toggle and a one-hour autoscale bump.
- Customer impact & ask: pilot customers experienced timeouts; Brightleaf is asking for visibility and remediation. For goodwill, the account team recommends offering a 25% usage credit for the 24-hour window while we validate stability.
- Approval request: sign-off to push the mux-disable to Brightleaf and permission to offer up to 25% credit for incident window. If leadership prefers, we can route them to a dedicated capacity pool (reserved) and draft a formal RCA later.

Please respond with quick thumb (approve) so we can communicate to Brightleaf.

Jordan Blake
Senior Manager, GTM Operations
From: Lauren Cho <laurencho@brightleafhealth.com>

Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast triage.

We're happy to try the mux-disable toggle and confirm whether our session stability improves. Please let us know the endpoint and expected cutover window. If you need us to route traffic to a fallback route, we can update our client config on short notice.

Also thanks for the proposed credit — the team is satisfied with the remediation path as long as we have a temporary mitigation and a follow-up RCA within 72 hours.

Lauren
Sr. Platform Engineer, Brightleaf Health
